Every pixel should earn its place. ## Background Our current website was built two years ago. It no longer reflects where we are as a company. Our product has matured, our audience has grown, and our brand has evolved. The site feels fragmented, loads slowly on mobile, and fails to communicate our core value proposition within the first five seconds. This redesign is not a facelift. It is a ground-up rethinking of how we show up online. ## Objectives - **Clarify the narrative**: A visitor should understand what we do, who it's for, and why it matters in under 10 seconds - **Increase conversion**: Improve free trial sign-up rate by 30% within 60 days of launch - **Elevate brand perception**: The site should feel premium, trustworthy, and unmistakably *us* - **Mobile-first performance**: Core Web Vitals in the top 10% of our category - **Enable the team**: Build on a flexible design system that marketing can update without engineering ## Target Audience ### Primary **The Pragmatic Decision-Maker** - Director / VP level - Evaluating tools for their team - Time-poor, skeptical of hype - Needs: credibility, clear ROI, fast answers ### Secondary **The Curious Practitioner** - Individual contributor - Researching solutions independently - Influenced by design quality & community - Needs: depth, docs, a reason to champion us internally ## Design Principles - **Clarity over cleverness**: If it needs explaining, simplify it - **Breathe**: Generous whitespace is not wasted space; it is confidence - **Motion with intention**: Animate to reveal meaning, never for decoration - **Type as personality**: Headlines carry the voice; body copy earns trust - **Accessible by default**: WCAG AA minimum, WCAG AAA where possible ## Scope of Work - **Homepage**: Complete redesign: hero, social proof, feature highlights, CTA - **Product overview**: New narrative arc, interactive feature exploration - **Pricing**: Simplify tiers, add comparison table, FAQ section - **About / Team**: Founder story, culture signal, team photography - **Blog / Resources hub**: New templates for articles, guides, changelogs - **Case studies**: Visual storytelling format, pull-quote emphasis ## Creative Direction > *"We want people to feel the product before they click a single button."* ### Mood & Tone The aesthetic lives at the intersection of **editorial clarity** and **product precision**: think a high-design magazine that also happens to ship software. Warm, not cold. Confident, not arrogant. Human, not generic. ### Visual Language - **Color**: Anchored in our brand navy and cream, with one punchy accent used sparingly for CTAs only - **Typography**: Large, expressive headlines (editorial serif) paired with a clean, legible sans for body - **Imagery**: Real product UI, real people, zero stock photos of people shaking hands in an office - **Illustration**: Abstract geometric forms where needed; no cartoon characters or flat icons - **Spacing**: 8pt grid. Consistent. Generous. ### Inspiration References - Linear: *precision and craft in motion* - Stripe: *trust through design consistency* - Vercel: *developer-grade clarity for a broad audience* ## Timeline
**Phase** **Dates** **Deliverables**
Discovery Week 1–2 Audit, competitive analysis, stakeholder interviews, design principles
Strategy & Architecture Week 3 Sitemap, content hierarchy, IA sign-off
Wireframes Week 4–5 Lo-fi wireframes for all P0 pages, stakeholder review
Visual Design Week 6–8 Hi-fi designs, design system components, motion spec
Handoff & Build Week 9–10 Dev handoff, QA, performance testing
Launch End of Q3 Go live, post-launch monitoring
## Success Metrics - **Bounce rate** below 45% on homepage - **Time to first meaningful interaction** under 3 seconds - **Free trial CVR** up 30% from current baseline - **Lighthouse performance score** 90 or above - **Brand perception survey** net positive shift in "modern" and "trustworthy" attributes ## Team & Responsibilities
Role Responsible For
Lead Designer Creative direction, visual design, design system
UX Researcher User interviews, usability testing, copy validation
Content Strategist Messaging framework, copy, SEO structure
Front-end Engineer Component build, performance, accessibility
Product Marketing Positioning, audience definition, launch
## Open Questions - Do we localize for launch or post-launch? - Is the blog migration in scope or handled separately by content team? - Video or static hero: TBD pending brand shoot availability
